digest.component_or_area: CI/build system — Gerrit Verified job orchestration and test execution
propositions: Ubuntu Verified jobs occupy 30.2 runner-minutes per run across three Python cells (py3.11/py3.12/py3.13) consuming 1,812 runner-seconds total, contributing to org-wide queue contention without coverage loss

Redundant YAML parse/loading in bridge cadence test invokes workflow schedule 1,440 times (measured 7.925s baseline, 0.001s cached), yielding 5.70 runner-minutes per Verified run via single hoist without changing exhaustive minute checks

Static golden Pandoc fixtures paired with small real-Pandoc contracts preserve ADR 0095 assertions while eliminating 883 redundant legacy subprocesses (measured 0.22s wall delta, hygiene not critical-path)
Editor fixture setup consumes 35.0-35.1s (socket.getfqdn threshold), identified as distributed CPU-bound DNS lookup under concurrent load rather than single subprocess

Same-change Gerrit Verify cancellation failed because job-level always() predicates re-evaluated true on superseding patchset, leaving stale run consuming runners for 25+ minutes; !cancelled() predicate repair stops obsolete jobs immediately

Post-remediation steady-state verified runs average 22–26 minutes end-to-end (inside 20–30 minute target), macOS 19–24 minutes critical path, with no individual test phase exceeding 30 seconds and 21% baseline-normalized Ubuntu occupancy reduction measured across multiple organic runs
